test_title: PYST 42: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 23 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides a right to profess, practice and propagate religion?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 25**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 25** of the Indian Constitution guarantees all individuals the freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion.
 
• This article is part of the **Fundamental Rights** under Part III of the Constitution, specifically ensuring religious freedom.
 
• The rights under Article 25 are subject to public order, morality, and health, and other provisions of Part III.
 
• It applies equally to all persons, irrespective of their religion, ensuring secularism as a core principle of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Article 25 also allows the state to regulate or restrict any economic, financial, political, or other secular activities associated with religious practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 26:** Provides the right to manage religious affairs, allowing religious denominations to establish institutions for religious and charitable purposes.
 
• **Article 27:** Prohibits compelling any person to pay taxes for the promotion or maintenance of any religion or religious institutions.
 
• **Article 28:** Addresses freedom as to attendance at religious instruction or religious worship in certain educational institutions.
 
• **Secularism in India:** Indian secularism guarantees the state’s neutrality towards all religions while allowing freedom of religious practices.
 
• **Restrictions on Article 25:** The state can intervene to regulate practices that contradict public order, morality, or health, or for social welfare reforms such as the abolition of untouchability or sati.
